executive_summary: This collection window (November 24 - 30, 2026) is the twenty-third archived window overall and the first to nominally cover actual Black Friday/Cyber Monday dates (Nov 27-30, 2026) rather than the retail calendar's early-access run-up. Fresh search again found no dated, sourced coverage of a CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund 2026 winner from CFDA, Vogue, WWD, Business of Fashion, or Fashionista -- available coverage remains limited to the June finalist announcement and the October 20 gala date. This is now the sixth consecutive window this signal has been carried forward open, and applying this archive's own is_prolonged_silence() check (four-or-more-consecutive-window threshold) against this signal_id's tracked history returns True as of last window and remains True here; this report's human_editor_note reflects that formal result rather than an informal 'still open' note. The CFDA Fashion Awards question was also re-checked with a fresh search, again finding no confirmed 2026 date, nominee list, or post-event coverage; this report formalizes that question as a tracked top_signals entry with its own signal_id for the first time (it was previously narrative-only in executive summaries and limitations, not machine-trackable), so is_prolonged_silence() cannot yet return True for it under this archive's own history mechanism even though five prior reports have informally called it open -- that gap between narrative claim and tracked history is itself noted below. Separately, this window's search specifically targeted post-event Black Friday/Cyber Monday 2026 sales-performance coverage, since last window's early-retail-calendar signal predicted the event would fall inside this window (Nov 27). Search did not surface genuine 2026 post-event results: pages nominally dated or titled 2026 either restated pre-event projections or reused prior-year (2025) National Retail Federation-sourced figures (e.g. the widely syndicated '202.9 million shoppers' and '$45.6B apparel' figures, which are 2025 holiday-weekend results, not 2026 ones) under 2026-tagged URLs and headlines. This is a known constraint of point-in-time web search rather than a finding about the event itself -- Black Friday/Cyber Monday 2026 did occur within this window per the retail calendar, but this report cannot verify its sales outcome with genuine in-window sourced coverage, so no sales-performance claim is made. The prior window's early-access retail-calendar signal is carried forward and updated to note only that the full event is now confirmed to have occurred within this window's dates, not what its results were. No other in-window garment, silhouette, or aesthetic discourse independently verifiable to this window was found. On balance this window remains thin, continuing the post-fashion-month quiet stretch, with one institutional signal now past this archive's own prolonged-silence threshold, a second institutional question newly formalized for tracking, and the retail-calendar signal updated but not resolved.
